ANSWER OF AI ABOUT THE SECOND BULLET POINT OF TASK1
Initial Scan of the Document Set
The document set covers research related to complex industrial production planning and scheduling, with a particular focus on steelmaking, furnace scheduling and energy efficiency. The papers address different parts of the steel production process, including reheating and heat-treatment furnaces, hot rolling, continuous casting, ladle operations and energy management. A smaller number of papers use related manufacturing environments to investigate comparable scheduling problems.
The initial scan shows why this is a complex knowledge domain. The scheduling problems involve multiple production stages, operational constraints, competing objectives and uncertainty. The documents consider objectives such as production efficiency, energy consumption, cost, tardiness and resource utilization, while also addressing changing conditions such as machine breakdowns, uncertain processing times, changing production requirements and fluctuating energy prices.
The document set brings a broad range of tools and approaches to these problems. These include mathematical optimization, heuristics and metaheuristics, robust and dynamic scheduling, forecasting and machine learning, reinforcement learning and multi-agent systems, digital twins and IoT, and explainable or human-centred AI.
The boundaries of the document set can therefore be described as the intersection of industrial production scheduling, energy efficiency and intelligent automation, primarily within steelmaking and furnace-related operations. The collection ranges from traditional optimization methods to newer data-driven and AI-based approaches for dynamic and increasingly automated decision-making.

THE ANSWER OF AI
The hierarchical topic tree maps the main knowledge contained in the document set. The literature is centred on industrial production scheduling and optimization, with strong branches in energy efficiency, optimization methods and intelligent automation. Further areas include digital twins, real-time decision-making and explainable/human-centred AI. The hierarchy shows that the document set combines the industrial application domain with a range of methods for optimizing and automating production decisions.
TASK 2.2

THE OUTPUT OF THE SECOND BULLET POINT
The cross-reference network shows that knowledge is most concentrated around production scheduling, optimization and energy efficiency. These topics are strongly interconnected, particularly within steel and furnace-related applications. AI and reinforcement learning connect scheduling with more adaptive and real-time decision-making, while digital twins provide a bridge between production data and intelligent scheduling. Explainable and human-centred AI form a smaller and more isolated part of the document set, although they connect to intelligent automation through the need to understand and interact with automated decisions. Overall, the network shows a progression from traditional optimization toward increasingly data-driven, adaptive and intelligent production systems.
